In this study, we establish a Liouville theorem for rigid dumu- $\left( R, \mathcal{S} \right)$ - $\tau$ - flows when the scalar curvature remains constant, extending a result previously established by the second author, who proved a liouville theorem for dumu flows with non-decreasing concavity under the condition that the scalar curvature is constant. Our confirmation of this conjecture allows us to derive the non-collapsing property for dumu flows with constant $\mathcal{R}$ and $\mathcal{K}$ - concavity, where $\mathcal{K}$ - concavity encompasses both $\mathcal{R}$ - concavity and $\mathcal{S}$ - concavity as special cases.

The primary objective of entry level tasks is to enable entry from highly under-resourced backgrounds into entry level tasks that are mastered by models with more resources. Entries can be achieved through parameter adjustments in existing models, with additional training data being an option. The utilization of extra data often requires creating new parameters and training them with the new data, as opposed to existing models that can be adjusted using their original parameters and data. Existing methods for entries with more resources include adjustments made when using more parameters or more data, as well as methods like ELLA and LEAPS that facilitate entries with minimal changes to the model's initial training. ELLA achieves this by creating a shared layer with the new task's model, while LEAPS does so by transferring selected layers. However, when using a large model as a base, ELLA and LEAPS require retraining the entire target model or part of it, respectively. Our proposed method, known as Dynamic Entrances (DE), aims to allow for entries into model tasks that are well-defined when there are significant differences in data distribution, by creating a separate global mean pooling layer with extra training data. The existing model's layers remain intact in the DE framework, in contrast to ELLA and LEAPS that require changing the model's layers. Our results from various experiments on synthetic and real-world tasks demonstrate that our approach outperforms ELLA and LEAPS in a wide range of scenarios.

In this research, a comparison is made between general relativity within the framework of precise parallax measurements, similar to those conducted by the Gaia satellite. Specifically, a new equation has been derived to describe the gravitational time dilation experienced by a detector on Earth due to the Sun's movement within the Milky Way and PPN parameter $\gamma$ that influences the impact of this gravitational time dilation on time interval measurements. This equation is further simplified under the condition that the distance to a star is significantly larger than the Schwarzschild radius of the Sun. Furthermore, precise parallax measurements are analyzed in relation to this equation to determine if precise measurements of these time intervals could theoretically provide support for general relativity. However, as shown in this study, the impact of solar gravitational time dilation on precise measurements of these intervals is too minimal to provide observational evidence for general relativity due to the uncertainty surrounding the PPN parameter $\gamma$. The derived equation may still offer value in improving precise PPN parameter $\gamma$ estimates by taking into account the influence of solar gravitational time dilation. Ultimately, this investigation highlights the intricate relationship between post-Newtonian physics, the movement of stars within the galaxy, and precise satellite-based astrometry.

Open-commonsense question-answering (QC) aims to generate meaningful explanations behind simple answer statements.  In open-domain QC, explaining the background knowledge that supports both the answer and the supporting text is a key challenge.  Due to the vast size of the knowledge base, retrieving specific pieces of information is a significant hurdle.  In this study, we address this challenge by developing a novel model called Coarse-to-Careful Semantic-connected Insight for Open-domain QC.  First, a cost-effective coarser model captures general background knowledge at a lower computational cost.  Next, a more precise careful model is trained to extract a more in-depth explanation.  In our proposed Coarse-to-Careful framework, both models are integrated to jointly respond to open-domain QC questions.  To further improve the coarser model's performance, we also designed a re-ranking mechanism to combine the two models effectively.  To assess the proposed method, we used the ReCoQ dataset and found that using both models together led to a 10.1 point improvement in R@10 over the best single model.  Additionally, the integrated framework achieved a 4.0 point gain in R@10 compared to the coarser model alone, and we discovered that a coarser model 0.7 times the size of the careful model yielded the most efficient and effective results.  To further explore the potential of coarse-to-caring strategy, we also extended the Coarse-to-Care

Astronomical observations have revealed a significant abundance of comets, and these celestial bodies are composed of small solid particles along with various molecular substances. Studies indicate that many of these molecules exist as positively charged ions, including prominent examples such as H2O+, CO+, and CO2+. To better understand the properties and behavior of these cometary molecules, it is crucial to develop a comprehensive set of radiation parameters, and to fill in the gaps in our current knowledge about the parameters of water, carbon dioxide, and carbon-containing molecular cations.

In the context of Federated Learning, a significant challenge posed by client heterogeneity, where clients with varying storage, computation, and data amounts participate in training, has been explored. A standard centralized ML approach becomes impractical for a single server to retain a combined dataset due to privacy concerns and the sensitive nature of the data. Nevertheless, a method called "Stroll for Education" (S4E) has been proposed to enable a server to learn a representative distribution of client data distributions through a random sampling process. S4E allows the server to generate a pseudo-client that behaves like a real client, with a data distribution that reflects the combined characteristics of the participating clients. This is achieved without the need for the server to know the details of the communication protocol, client data sizes, or the presence of malicious clients. The effectiveness of S4E has been shown in multiple real-world FL applications, where it allows for more efficient training on diverse client data sets, improving the server's access to a broader range of data and reducing communication costs.

Mandatory counseling in prisons is supposed to improve inmates' mental health, but its effects are unclear. This study investigates the impact of required counseling on the general well-being of criminals in Georgia. It finds that participating in counseling significantly enhances mental health, reduces depression, and increases life satisfaction among prisoners, with these improvements persisting even after release. These findings suggest that counseling's beneficial effects are long-lasting and translate into real-world benefits, such as better physical health, reduced substance abuse, and increased employment rates post-release. The study also explores variations in counseling's impact, finding that its effects are more pronounced for younger prisoners and those with prior convictions, likely due to their greater potential for post-release society reintegration.

Medical image segmentation is a crucial step in diagnosing and treating various conditions, yet it can be made more challenging due to limited data, a common issue in clinical settings. To overcome this challenge, a new technique called SART has been developed, which combines a complex, accurately trained model with a simple, initially inconsistent one. By taking the data-driven SART approach, the technique aims to improve the overall results of semi-supervised medical image segmentation. An examination of several semi-supervised and fully supervised scenarios across multiple complex datasets reveals that SART consistently delivers superior results compared to other recent regularization methods.

Lévy flights represent random movements where individual components move in varying distances and directions, with significant strides occurring more frequently than probability theory predicts. Researchers believe chaotic behaviors, such as Lévy flights, are widespread in both natural and artificial settings. However, traditional methods for measuring complexity often fail to account for these behaviors due to their reliance on predictable, linear patterns. This study introduces a novel, machine learning-based approach utilizing graph neural networks to predict future movements and detect the chaotic nature of a single entity's movement, successfully identifying the complex, unpredictable nature of a fruit fly's flight path and distinguishing it from straightforward linear movements.

Consider a set of $n$ complex numbers $z_1, \dots, n$ with non-zero imaginary components, where each $z_j$ corresponds to a specific parameter in a distribution $F$. The problem of estimating the distribution $F$ is tackled using the Generalized Maximum Likelihood (GML) method based on observed data $t_1, \dots, t_n$. A novel GML estimator for the mean of the parameters $\mu_z$ is developed and characterized as equivalent to a weighted geometric average of the parameters $z_j$, with a proof of consistency provided. Furthermore, the estimator demonstrates robustness against outliers and is contrasted with a traditional likelihood-based approach for estimating $\mu_z$. The effectiveness of the estimator is validated through Monte Carlo simulations, and it is also applied to address challenges in sampling theory.

Knowledge tracing has a significant impact on personalized education, and numerous deep learning models have been developed to analyze student performance and forecast future responses. Although several research papers on this topic have been published, obtaining and processing real-world datasets for evaluation has proven difficult due to the intricate data formats used in knowledge tracing. To address this challenge, we present PyKT, a comprehensive Python framework designed to facilitate the deployment of deep learning-based knowledge tracing systems using real-world datasets. This framework handles data preprocessing, commonly used models, and the Metric known as "Koussas Metric" to assess predictive accuracy. PyKT includes ready-to-use KT models that can be easily applied to raw data, and we have also made available KT-trained models for specific datasets to serve as benchmarks. To further assist the community, we have made the PyKT framework and associated documentation available online at GitHub.

Given a vector field X and a differential operator Δ both either elliptic or locally solvable, we prove that the range of X+Δ is closed in C∞(M). This result holds true for manifolds M, as well as for more complex structures like complex manifolds and algebraic varieties. Additionally, a refined version is established for algebraic varieties, taking into account polynomial growth.

To streamline effective automated reasoning, integrating downstream applications like code analysis benefits significantly from relying on external proofs generated by robust SMT solvers. This approach utilizes the high functionality of these applications while taking advantage of the comprehensive libf2py Rust bindings for the F2 pseudo-TPATP proof format. However, one challenge lies in the lack of widespread adoption of Rust among proponents of modular reasoning tools. To overcome this barrier, we developed Alethe, an alternative proof format featuring C bindings and already finding a number of users. We further enhanced Alethe by incorporating Rust and added support for the F2 format. This paper presents the details of Alethe and explains its design decisions in depth.

In federated learning, synchronous training is commonly used to combine model updates from multiple clients.  The efficiency of this process is largely determined by how models are aggregated in a coordinated process.  The success of this approach is largely dependent on the nature of the information it conveys, specifically whether it is unconstrained or uninformative.  The notion of being uninformative has been extensively researched, whereas the potential of being unconstrained remains largely untapped.  The challenge of working with constrained data is also well-established, whereas the challenges posed by the uninformative are less apparent.  This paper explores the characteristics of the informative and unconstrained data in the context of the synchronous approach to federated learning, specifically the fully coordinated and buffered methods.  The theorems derived from this research reveal the conditions under which the data is considered uninformative or unconstrained.  The nature of the perturbations that result in uninformative and unconstrained data are also examined, whereas those that lead to informative and constrained data are contrasted, respectively.  The theorems derived from this research are further illustrated with the help of concrete examples, whereas previous results on the informative data are reviewed.  The implications of these results are also discussed in the context of designing a more effective buffered aggregation process for the future.

The primary goal of data augmentation in deep learning is to enhance a model's ability to generalize by artificially increasing the size of a dataset. A common approach to augmenting speech data involves using an automatic speech recognition system's confidence scores and word-level probabilities from its most probable predictions to either accept or reject certain sentences, thereby selecting high-quality training sentences for a target task. However, the current practice of utilizing ASR-generated translations to directly augment parallel corpora for machine translation is widely criticized due to the necessity of manually translating low-confidence sentences and the risk of introducing biases from the accepted sentences. In this study, we explore the use of such ASR-generated translations to bridge the gap between a well-annotated source language and a scarce target language, specifically to facilitate the training of neural machine translation models. Our approach leverages a foreign language written in a non-standard orthography and demonstrates that utilizing ASR-generated translations between English and the foreign language significantly improves NMT model performance, particularly when the target language data is limited. The proposed method yields substantial improvements in NMT models, outperforming those trained solely on standard written forms of the language, as evidenced by our results.

Achieving effective navigation for underwater robots requires them to accurately detect obstacles in their path. However, underwater environments often contain dynamic elements, such as floating debris, which can change over time and pose challenges for the robots' navigation capabilities. To address this issue, this study develops a method based on Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) that enables robots to learn about the sparseness of their environment and prioritize areas with higher obstacle density for further investigation. By focusing on regions with higher density, the robots can efficiently explore and update their models using less data than would be necessary with non-sparse learning approaches. This study evaluates the proposed method in both simulated and real-world scenarios, comparing it to established baselines and demonstrating improved performance in navigating dynamic environments with floating debris.

We've extended our recent single-fluid celestial body model to include a more complex, non-uniform two-fluid distribution in General Relativity. A celestial body is described as non-uniform when its symmetry follows the $SO(2,1)\times U(1)$ Killing vector field, and its matter content adheres to a specific equation of state. Using a $U(2,1)\times U(1)$ covariant 1+1+2 kinematic approach, we've expanded our earlier single-fluid model to encompass two distinct species of matter. The resulting two-fluid distribution leads to the Tolman IV solution when a dominant energy condition is applied. Furthermore, we've developed a boundary value problem to determine a non-singular stellar object within this two-framework, and we've applied this approach to a binary neutron star system modeled as two concentric celestial bodies.

Most current machine translation accuracy improvement methods rely on abundant data within new domains, yet this is often not the case in real-life scenarios. In this study, a more efficient approach is proposed that can enhance grammar correction models and transfer successfully to new language varieties with limited data, even just a single paragraph. A simple but effective strategy is used to transfer data, matching erroneous words with correct ones, and the effects on model performance are tested through multiple grammar error rectification domain transfer tasks. This performance is better than current approaches, particularly when there's only a small amount data in the target domain.

This study examines the efficiency of pure Nash equilibria in a resource allocation setting where agents are indifferent between available resources and can act strategically. We find that for any number of possible equilibria, there exists a scenario in which the resulting resource distribution is worse than a greedy approach in at least one dimension. We also establish upper limits for the ratio between the welfare of the worst and a fair-division benchmark, discovering that for two dimensions, the worst-case ratio is 4/3, and for more than two dimensions, the ratio is 2 - 2/f, where f is the number of dimensions.

The discovery of an extremely compact, stable disk at the center of galaxy UGC 8839 using Very Long Baseline Interferometry is an unprecedented finding.  This very small, non-emissive disk, measuring less than 400 astronomical units in diameter, remains enigmatic. Its origin is attributed to the interaction between a supermassive black hole and very low mass stars in a close orbit, or potentially to the remnant of an accretion disk from the galaxy's formation.  The discovery of such minuscule, non-active structures around supermassive black holes has significant implications for both radio astronomy and the study of galaxy evolution.

Alloysing two-current representations of hadronic vacuum polarization inputs 
concerning pions allows for numerical verification of key relations in QCD. 
When calculating P and T components of the vacuum polarization from pions, 
discrepancies arise in the two-current formulations, specifically the Boernstein- 
Wilczek and Posner-Posner relationships fail for the P and T components 
separately, requiring redefinition with new two-pion correlators, sigma_p(t) 
and delta_p(t). 
This study establishes the sigma_p(t) and delta_p(t) functions through 
real-time lattice QCD calculations of the hadronic vacuum polarization.

Recent advancements in optical and IR photometry have significantly expanded our knowledge of young stellar objects' variability. In this research, a high-resolution dataset comprising 10,454 optical/IR photometric points has been utilized to analyze the accretion rates and physical characteristics of the young star XX Cha over a three-year period. Both the spectral energy distribution and the variability have been modeled in detail, revealing significant short-term fluctuations in the X-ray flux and continuum excess variability that directly impact the fluctuations in the accretion rate. Furthermore, an unusually low minimum accretion rate of $10^{-10}$ M$_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$ has been discovered in XX Cha, which is at least two orders of magnitude lower than previously observed in this system and extends the known range of accretion rate variability by two orders of magnitude. These fluctuations are likely linked to changes in the disk's inner structure, and their effects are particularly pronounced in the system's brightness fluctuations across different wavelength ranges.

Offline reinforcement learning has been successfully applied to tackle complex multi-agent interactions. However, a critical issue arises when trained models are evaluated through joint environmental evaluation, as the assessment relies on both absolute and relative performance, which can be discouraging for agents. To address this challenge, we investigate a novel offline relative setting where only the relative performance of an agent is considered, and if an agent outperforms its competitor, its policy is positively reinforced. Surprisingly, this setup presents a distinct learning challenge as effective agents are unlikely to be included in the data, and any given state may have only favorable or unfavorable experiences. Despite these limitations, we demonstrate the relevance of this problem in practical applications and provide an in-depth analysis of its underlying mechanics. To move forward, we propose a parametric approach that leverages effective offline algorithms to solve this problem. To validate our solution, we conduct extensive experiments and compare our proposed method with baseline methods, and the results indicate significant performance gains.

We investigate the use of 2D/3D image alignment using megavoltage images in a convolutional neural network framework. Our approach combines a feature extractor and deformable architecture, utilizing only shallow network depth and training. The developed model demonstrates a significant improvement in accurate image registration compared to traditional methods, with reduced mean and maximum displacement errors of 1.1mm and 2.4mm, respectively.

The fundamental role of single-particle entanglement in guiding particles and resulting in nonlocal phenomena has been debated for decades. Here, we demonstrate that the entanglement of a single particle indeed leads to nonlocal phenomena by employing the nonlocal guidance theory. By utilizing the steering effect in a loose Bell test scenario with the Greenberger-Horne-Shelly-Zahner (GHZ) effect, we show that even minimal levels of single-particle entanglement can produce a nonlocal guidance signal in the absence of interactions. Moreover, we show that guidance effect magnitudes can be used to quantify the nonlocal character of single-particle states.

Educational systems have significantly advanced through the integration of IoT technology over the last few years. The forthcoming convergence of federated learning and blockchain technology could further revolutionize these IoT-based educational frameworks. In response, this paper conducts an exhaustive survey of educational systems for Internet of Vehicles (IoV) that utilize federated learning to safeguard student data privacy and employ blockchain to enhance the security and transparency of educational transactions. The primary focus of this review is on critical aspects including the BloV2F framework's applicability to IoV, potential improvements, proposed future educational models, and possible licensing and royalty issues associated with the use of blockchain technology. Ultimately, this paper outlines potential future research directions for the development of more robust IoV educational systems.

V392 Persei, a nova that exhibited higher-than-normal \gamma-ray emissions during its 2014 outburst, is the subject of this report. V392 Persei was initially classified as a new star in 2014, but was later identified as an optical variable. During its peak of the 2014 outburst, it temporarily brightened by 4.5 magnitudes. Observations across multiple wavelengths allowed for the construction of a comprehensive model to explain the observed phenomena. V392 Persei is a single star system consisting of a white dwarf and a main sequence companion. The system is binary with a 10.4-day period and is open to the interstellar medium around it. The white dwarf accreted hydrogen-rich material and reached a critical mass, leading to a Type 1 nova outburst on its surface. The observed \gamma-ray emission was caused by the acceleration of protons in the inner part of the accretion disk and the subsequent interaction of these protons with the surrounding cloud. V392 Persei is among the most luminous nova systems in the universe and is now the second such system to be observed. The fact that V392 Persei is a known variable star and has a well-studied system makes it an ideal candidate for future studies.

A new method for precoder selection and encoding is proposed, drawing inspiration from Gaussian Mixture Models. In this proposed technique, reference signals are viewed as a vector representing a single dimension of a actual vector with multiple dimensions. These actual vectors form a cluster that embodies a specific precoder's codebook entry. In effect, the system now comprises a two-stage encoder, with one stage selecting a cluster and the other selecting a specific point within the chosen cluster. This proposed method replaces the traditional approach of treating reference signals as scalar values. Numerical simulations show that the new method provides a consistent performance boost of 0.5 to 1 bits/s/Hz across various scenarios, utilizing only existing resources and signaling.

We perform precise numerical simulations to analyze the robustness of a particular type of stable nonequilibrium behavior in a 2D system that doesn't reach thermal equilibrium. This system consists of electrons moving on the surface of a 3D cubic structure and subject to a strong, varying magnetic field. The characteristics of these electrons display strong localization in both ordinary and extreme magnetic conditions. The localization patterns in their energy bands exhibit direct and fractional quantum Hall effects in the surface current that results from the agitation of the particle ensemble. The stability of this nonequivalent distribution of surface currents is found to be highly resistant to the intensity of the magnetic field, the way the cubic structure is arranged, and the introduction of disordered conditions.

For a star deeply embedded in a dense stellar cluster's center, the pace of a star growing by feeding on surrounding stars and gas is believed to be restricted by the physics of a star-capture process known as Bondi accretion rates. This study aims to establish the maximum speed of this type of accretion by developing a more refined understanding of Bondi accretion rates. By incorporating the effects of velocity distributions and expanding beyond the initial approximation of a two-body interaction, we have created an improved theoretical model of ACCRETING STAR dynamics. When applied to specific velocity distributions and stellar evolution models, this enhanced framework can either accelerate or decelerate ACCRETING STAR growth compared to the classic Bondi accretion rate predictions, but in no scenario does it exceed approximately three times the initial pace. Additionally, this study demonstrates how density fluctuations caused by a running star can be integrated into the accretion rate equations, further limiting the maximum pace of ACCRETING STAR growth to well below the initial Bondi accretion rates. These findings provide a more constrained and realistic upper boundary for ACCRETING STAR growth pace before it becomes visible and offer valuable insights for the exploration of extreme stars in various astronomical settings.

The presence of dense star clusters with a high concentration of massive stars at the centers of galaxies is a longstanding mystery. One proposed explanation is that these groups could be made up of remnant objects like neutron stars and black holes, which are much harder to detect through traditional means. The unique microgravity environment of these star clusters may cause the Initial Mass Unseen Stars to produce gravitational waves through two processes: the gradual distortion of the stars during binary interactions and the sudden bursts generated by binary mergers. The intensity of gravitational waves from these events can be precisely calculated and predicted, providing the possibility that the IceCube, LIGO, Virgo, and KAGRA detectors could have already picked up the signals from these objects. The characteristics of these detections would be distinct from their usual sources, particularly in terms of the continuous gravitational waves that could be identified by their specific patterns.

In this paper, we investigate the physical layer security of wireless communication systems using amplitude/frequency selection relaying with two full-duplex relays. A proposed relaying selection protocol is presented to identify and eliminate interference caused by relays with compromised links. The paper also compares our protocol to an optimal selection protocol and reveals that the protocol offers the same level of physical layer security while offering better knowledge of the system. Furthermore, we derive the exact and approximate throughputs of the system to provide in-depth performance analysis.

Text-based adventure games, rich in narrative depth, offer an uncomplicated and effective means to achieve a sophisticated one million moves per second benchmark in agent simulation. Our research reveals that such narrative-driven environments can produce a substantial one million seconds of agent training equivalent to training one million AI agents simultaneously. We also demonstrate the one million moves per second benchmark achievement on TextWorldExpress, a simplified version of one million plus sentences text-based adventure games, while maintaining the richness of the narrantive elements.

A video stream comprises a multitude of data points, making sequence analysis a computationally intensive task. Deep learning methods, particularly Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, have been widely used for sequence analysis due to their high performance, despite their power-intensive nature. To address this challenge, this paper presents a novel approach that combines an LSTM-based algorithm for sequence prediction with a hardware design that leverages the unique properties of Hilbert-Tucker tensor decompresison to significantly reduce storage requirements and increase data accessibility speed. The proposed system's performance is evaluated through various prediction tasks, comparing it to conventional LSTM hardware and demonstrating its superior efficiency in terms of memory usage, access speed, and processing performance. The paper also provides a detailed hardware implementation of the proposed architecture, offering a comprehensive and practical solution for sequence analysis applications.

We explore the concept of the "gravity conjecture" within the context of scalar fields in theories of gravity, formulating a more comprehensive version that encompasses all charged objects, not just particles. A key component of this revised gravity conjecture is the assertion of convexity, suggesting that the combined charge of objects in certain conformal field theories exhibits a property of mathematical convexity when a specific distance measure is applied. This measure, inspired by the swampland distance conjecture, relies on the parameters defining the theory and remains meaningful even when applied to complex combinations of charged objects. To support or refute our hypothesis, we provide several illustrative examples and explore the underlying rationale for the proposed refined gravity conjecture.

A polynomial that captures the behavior of the Hilbert function of a graded algebra is known as the Hilbert polynomial. When considering the blow-up algebra of an ideal in a Noetherian ring, a polynomial analogous to the Hilbert polynomial is called the compact Hilbert polynomial. Recently introduced by S. Goto, K. Shibata, and M. C. Unangst, this concept is now applied to the study of F-singularities in commutative algebra. Specifically, it is demonstrated that the Hilbert function of the associated graded algebra with respect to the test ideal of a local ring with a good singular behavior is equivalent to a particular compact polynomial under certain conditions. This, in turn, implies that the associated graded algebra has the same finiteness properties as the test ideal under those conditions. Moreover, when applied to Gorenstein local rings with F-singularities, it is shown that the associated graded algebra with respect to the maximal ideal also shares these properties. This, in turn, implies that the corresponding graded algebra has the same F-purity singularities behavior as the original ring and that its a-invariant can be calculated.

The integration of auxiliary services in energy market reformation is a critical step in ensuring grid stability and reliability. Given the regional variations in primary energy sources, energy systems are highly interconnected, underscoring the need for robust transmission systems. The transmission system operators are in the process of developing new market engagement strategies to bolster transmission system reliability and reduce dependence on fossil fuels and nuclear energy. These emerging strategies require energy system experts to evaluate their long-term effects on the overall energy system. To meet this challenge, the Energy System Analysis group at the University of Stuttgart has developed a comprehensive procurement model for auxiliary services that takes into account market engagements, with the goal of providing a detailed example of how energy system analyses can be used to assess the energy system impacts of new market engagement strategies for auxiliary services.

Let $f$ and $g$ be coprimally related functions with at least one not a constant. We define $W_n(f,g)$ as the $n$-th Wittstein heap resulting from $n$ iterations of the Laplace transformation on the field of rational functions $\Klangle z\rangle$. In this investigation, we aim to determine conditions under which a prime function $P$ can divide $W_n(f,g)$ for all instances of $n$ in the natural numbers after it divides the original product $f \cdot g$. An illustration is provided where $W_n$ is derived from the Chebychev polynomials.

Saturn's polar atmosphere is experiencing significant changes as temperatures rise near the summer pole, potentially indicating the onset of a polar vortex. Observations from various sources, including the Ultraviolet Imaging Spectrograph on the Cassini spacecraft, reveal the gradual development of a pentagonal shape that may signal a transition to a polar vortex in the northern hemisphere. However, observations of the 20 stratospheric temperatures and winds over the past six years lack evidence of a 11-year solar cycle influence and differ from expected seasonal patterns. As the planet approaches its summer solstice, scientists anticipate a possible outbreak of a polar vortex in the northern stratosphere.

This study investigates the Schrödinger equation with a convex external potential and no damping mechanism, specifically in a two-dimensional space and beyond. It is shown that, under certain conditions, the system is prone to explosions, where the particle's density grows indefinitely at a particular point in a finite amount of time. This conclusion stands in contrast to the system's behavior in an enclosed environment, where the density field is guaranteed to remain bounded. To support our main finding, we develop an analytical approach and also use numerical simulations to corroborate them.

This work explores the development of local Abbreviation Operators in the context of a specific type of algebraic structure. It begins by defining a class of operators that preserve another property within varieties over a particular kind of algebra, denoted as A. In contrast to various existing research, which primarily focuses on characteristic zero, this study extends its investigation to include cases where the characteristic is positive. The Operators in question lead to various results, including various embedding theorems for various types of algebraic structures over A, including topological algebras, algebras over algebras, and universal algebras, among others, in the positive characteristic setting.

In the context of persistence modules, a collection is a specific type of structure that corresponds to a module with tame dimension. These collections have a property of being Tiling with a 2-dimensional persistence diagram when restricted to 1-dimensional persistence modules. A method has been developed to polarize collections, which are generally not graded, into corresponding graded collections. A relationship has also been identified between the original collection and its polarized form.

This informal note discusses key aspects of local arithmetic measurements, specifically dealing with the definition of orbital integrals and the standardization of measures on manifolds associated with algebraic structures. We examine various measures used in literature, including those found in Bump's work on classical groups, Waldspurger's articles on central simple algebras, and the text from Tate on $p$-adic fields.

This research investigates how to employ soft X-ray scattering techniques to enhance the sensitivity of nuclear phase retrieval, which is crucial for interpreting nuclear scattering data and avoiding misinterpretation in x-ray absorption and refraction phenomena. By developing a modified scattering equation that takes into account a few-particle susceptibility, we found that the reliable range for accurate phase determination using X-ray techniques is narrower than previously thought. Nonetheless, we demonstrate through both numerical simulations and a physical experiment that the technique remains effective even outside this narrower range. Our findings provide actionable advice for optimizing x-ray spectroscopy methods and highlight the value of using x-ray techniques to calibrate the minute phase information required to precisely determine the position of x-ray absorption edges.

A new approach for single-phase Darcy flow in fractured and continuous rock formations is presented, building on existing hybrid and discontinuous finite element methods. This technique utilizes a specific element that combines a $Q_1$ continuous polynomial for pressure and vector-based boundary fluxes defined at the nodes and quadrature points of the element's integration. The element passes an integration test and ensures compatibility between mass fluxes on shared element boundaries, thus eliminating numerical non-physical oscillations in pressure. This technique has no integration reduction requirements, allows larger time-step sizes in time-dependent simulations, and yields more accurate results than traditional techniques, particularly in highly conductive fractures where it matches the accuracy of a more complex multi-field method. This approach is computationally efficient, producing similar accuracy to the rigorous multi-method at a significantly lower cost.

The Bayes Factor stands out as a robust statistical method for hypothesis testing, effectively circumventing many limitations of conventional testing methods. Despite its numerous advantages, the Bayes Factor has not gained widespread adoption in the statistical community. A potential reason for this underutilization is the computational complexity of implementing it, particularly in scenarios involving multiple models and large datasets. However, a study utilizing synthetic data reveals that a systematic approach can be developed to calculate Bayes Factors efficiently, even when working with substantial datasets and numerous models. This study also highlights the utility of R packages such as `BayesFactor` and `brms` in achieving these computational goals. Ultimately, the Bayes Factor emerges as a viable option for large-scale Bayesian analyses, particularly in the context of Bayesian model checking and comparison.

This work focuses on a task called discourse indicator semantic analysis, which aims to automatically achieve a high level of abstraction in the semantic representation of discourse indicators. These indicators, such as "because," "however," and "finally," play a crucial role in helping readers grasp the underlying logical structure of a text. Although extensively researched and utilized in various applications, there has been no standardized method for evaluating the capacity of languages, including English, to represent the semantic structure ofIndicators. In this project, we established a dataset comprising 11,000 examples that mapIndicators to more complex semantic structures, utilizing the Berkeley Natural Language Inference dataset as a foundation. In addition, we developed a baseline approach leveraging the Natural Language Inferencing task and conducted a comprehensive examination of the indicators' semantic utility. In our research, we leveraged Indicators to enhance the interpretability of machine-generated narratives, demonstrating their effectiveness in representing the underlying logical structure of a text. In contrast, a range of more complex semantic frameworks failed to effectively represent theIndicators' underlying meaning in the context of a natural language inference task. In addition, we discovered that language models excel at identifying theIndicators'Indicators within a wide array of textual genres and lengths of passages.

Matrix decomposition is a fundamental technique in scientific research and data analysis. Recent studies have established that convexity is not a necessary condition for efficient optimization. Specifically, the concept of geodesic convexity has been shown to underpin the complexity of various nonconvex optimization problems, including matrix decomposition. This paper delves deeper into the geodesic convexity of nonconvex functions in the context of matrix decomposition, providing a comprehensive theory of nonconvex optimization. We prove that the nonconvex function surrounding the minimum of a general matrix decomposition problem is geodesically convex within a "ball" with a radius of 0.25 times the smallest distance between problem difficulty peaks. Furthermore, we show that functions with multiple difficulty peaks are geodesically convex beyond their respective peaks. These findings offer a novel perspective on the nonconvex functions that have worldwide minimum landscapes from both mathematical and optimization perspectives. Based on this geodesic convexity property, we propose a geodesic Newton method that guarantees finding a desired solution within a polynomial number of iterations, thus providing an efficient solution for general low-rank matrix optimization problems.

A graph is considered 3-colorable if a valid 3-coloring can be applied to it. A more stringent criterion, known as robust cubic 3-colorability, is met when the graph remains 3-colorable even when a subset of its edges is disregarded, as long as the remaining subgraph has an low degree. While all tree structures are recognized as robust cubic 3-colorable, this study presents a distinct example that is not a tree but exhibits the same characteristic. This unique finding is not attainable through the combination of previously established results.

Co-evolutionary algorithms are a powerful tool for resolving complex optimization problems in game theory. In this research, two co-evolutionary methods are developed and compared to determine the Nash Equilibrium in a symmetrical Cournot game. In these algorithms, each player's strategy is encoded within a distinct genetic population. Initially, the algorithm creates two separate populations of chromosomes, with each representing a player's production decision under various market conditions. As the simulation progresses, the fitness of each chromosome is assessed based on its performance against the opposing player's population, with the most successful strategies being passed on to the next generation. To further enhance the efficiency of these algorithms, two modifications are implemented to reduce the number of games played and accelerate the speed of the Co-NEGA/TGA algorithm. The results obtained from these six variations of co-evolutionary approaches are contrasted with existing results achieved through traditional evolutionary methods, with one modified algorithm demonstrating the highest effectiveness in reaching the Nash Equilibrium.

Let G=(V,E) be a directed graph without multiple edges or self-loops, and let I_G represent the edge ideal of G, a specific type of ideal within the polynomial ring K[V]. This study investigates the associated ideal (I_G)_*. In the context of directed graphs, we provide a method for calculating the minimal generators of the associated ideal (I_G)_*. It is further demonstrated that if the set of directed edges in G forms a symmetric relation, then the associated ideal (I_G)_* is reduced to its square root, which is generated by all individual variables, indicating that (I_G)_* possesses a symbolic depth of infinity. Additionally, we establish connections between the arithmetic properties of the associated ideal (I_G)_* and those of the ideal of the skew-symmetric graph associated with G, including the fact that the associated regularity and the associated depth of I_G are equal to those of I_H for the corresponding skew-symmetric graph H.

A significant challenge in deploying machine learning models in safety-critical applications is ensuring the reliability and trustworthiness of the system. Neural networks, particularly those trained via backpropagation, are prone to errors caused by both deliberate attacks and inadvertent hardware malfunctions, which can lead to incorrect predictions. This paper investigates the effectiveness of a proactive countermeasure, activation range monitoring, in ensuring the resilience of a critical object detection system against deliberate input manipulation and inadvertent memory address randomization. The system's performance under these conditions is thoroughly evaluated through rigorous testing, and the results indicate that a combination of a limited bit-width and a narrow monitoring range can effectively prevent deliberate misclassification while also tolerating a high rate of address errors with minimal impact on the system's accuracy. The findings of this study provide a solid foundation for the development of hardware failure-resilient machine learning systems, emphasizing the importance of a comprehensive testing framework to validate the countermeasure's efficacy.

The Jordanian twist, first introduced in 1996, is a deformation of the co-Frobenius structure that has been extensively researched in recent years due to its relevance in the context of quantum group representations. However, existing studies have treated the parameter as a generic constant, neglecting its inherent inherent nature. In this study, we investigate the impact of a varying parameter on the Jordanian twist, leading to the identification of a one-parameter family of Jordanian twists with distinct properties. Our analysis reveals that the Jordan twist, modified by this parameter family, results in altered reciprocity laws and obstructs the applicability of the Reshetikhin-Turaev construction for obtaining a semi-simple category from the representation category. These findings have been supported by numerical evidence obtained through direct computation.

A universal language model that encompasses multiple languages and facilitates a cluster of words with shared meaning has been highly sought after in the field of NLP. Such a ULM would enable researchers to conduct NLP tasks across different languages with greater efficiency and would also make studying low-resource languages more manageable by leveraging the knowledge of well-established languages. Despite its potential, creating a multi-lingual shared semantic framework remains a challenging task. We investigate a significant obstacle in this process: the discrepancy in word spaces across languages, which results from training embeddings independently for each language. This issue causes difficulties in aligning the different word spaces and leads to increased complexity in learning a mapping function. To address this challenge, we propose a novel, unsupervised, and multi-lingual framework that generates a common representation space for a set of languages. This approach, known as Cluster-consistent Word Representation (CWR), involves creating embeddings for each language and then generating a language-specific frame that preserves the local structure of the word space while ensuring that the resulting clusters of words are mutually congruent. We then combine these frames into a single, unified representation that serves as our multi-lingual framework. We further demonstrate the effectiveness of CWR by applying it to a variety of NLP tasks, including machine translation, pseudo-parallel data generation, and question answering. Our results indicate that CWR successfully establishes a common semantic framework across multiple languages that can be effectively utilized for a range of NLP tasks.

This research analyzes particle production in 5.44 TeV Xe-Xe collisions, focusing on pions, kaons, (anti-)protons, and $\phi$ mesons, using data from the ALICE experiment. At midrapidity, approximately 97.8 TeV of net energy is radiated as these particles, with 85% being pions. The average transverse momentum of these hadrons is 0.76, 1.0, 2.7, and 1.0 GeV/c for $\phi$ mesons, protons, kaons, and pions, respectively. In the intermediate rapidity region, collective flow effects are evident in the transverse momentum spectra of these hadrons. By fitting a hydro model, the initial collisions are found to occur within a very short timeframe of 6-7 fs/c, with an initial collision area of 75-80 $\text{fm}^2$. The initial temperature is estimated to be 4.0 $\pm$ 0.1 (stat) $\pm$ 0.2 (sys) GeV/c.

In late October 2019, Chile experienced widespread unrest and violence that lasted for nearly a month, resulting in numerous fatalities and injuries, extensive property damage, and the temporary closure of key infrastructure. This study presents a mathematical model of the protests' progression across the country, incorporating the transmission mechanisms observed and identifying three primary drivers: the initial spark in Santiago, a secondary ignition in Antofagasta, and the subsequent reactivation of Santiago. A comparative analysis of various outbreak scenarios was also simulated, taking into consideration the presence of a second focus in Antofagasta. Furthermore, the effects of policy interventions were quantified, demonstrating how they could slow the protests' spread and mitigate their duration. The study highlights the utility of such models in providing evidence-based guidance for emergency management and resource allocation during periods of intense social upheaval.

Given two sets of input words, defined by over a finite alphabet and described using Brzozowski quotient expressions, the study aims to efficiently verify their inclusion relation. A semi-algorithm is proposed to accomplish this, leveraging automatic techniques for solving satisfaction problems. Given two words and additional constraints, including recognized languages, defined by regular expressions, the algorithm determines if the first word can transition to the second through the state machine representing the inequality's satisfaction. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through the integration of this technique into a tool, known as BrzEx, and its application to resolving the open problem of Brzozowski conjecture for the over a finite alphabet.

This study investigates the numerical solution to a source completion problem in Maxwell's equations. Given partial measurements of the electric and magnetic fields at a specific time and within a given domain, the objective is to determine the missing information. Once the data is fully known, a solution is guaranteed to exist and be unique. To ensure stability, existence, and a level of smoothness in the solution, this paper employs a regularization approach based on the quasi-reversibility method. This involves formulating a perturbed problem, proving the existence and uniqueness of a solution, and establishing convergence to the true solution as certain parameters approach their limiting values. To demonstrate the technique's effectiveness, several two-dimensional numerical examples are presented.

When combining knowledge from multiple sources, it's often more effective than starting from scratch due to limitations in source data size, complexity, and the need for additional annotation. This work explores a setting where multiple knowledge graphs, which are structurally independent of one another, should be integrated into a single, interconnected knowledge graph. A federated learning approach is used to develop a neural relationship classifier that can be shared across knowledge graphs, while preserving data privacy. The classifier is trained in a federated setting using the knowledge triples from each graph, with the model parameters being aggregated in a secure manner. To achieve more accurate results, a novel method called Federated Discriminative Aggregation for Knowledge Integration is developed, which incorporates inter-graph connections as virtual triples to serve as additional training data. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is demonstrated through comprehensive experiments on both real-world and synthetic datasets, showing significant improvements in integrated knowledge and model performance when compared to existing baseline methods.

Maeda's conjecture suggests that the possible values of the second central moment, represented by the norm of the second Fourier coefficient of a normalized, cuspidal Hecke eigenform, should form a continuous set of natural numbers within the field of rational numbers. A significant effort to investigate this is finding polynomial pairs that can generate the second coefficient's value. This paper focuses on calculating the rank of the elliptic curves derived from quadratic and biquadratic decompositions of the second central moment for two specific non-abelian quartic groups, A4 and S4. Additionally, it presents data on the distribution of elliptic curves with rank -1, 0, 1, or 2 across these two fields.

In the context of relativistic quantum field theory, a local measurement's inability to significantly influence a distant entangled region's size is a key concept, expressed as the entanglement pressure law. This concept finds a concrete realization within the holographic principle, leading to the derivation of lower bounds on the entanglement pressure in terms of the entanglement's rate of change and acceleration, and ultimately, in terms of the Riemann tensor. Within the cosmological constant theory, specific instances of this law are calculated, including their connections to the quantum null energy condition and its implications for the dark energy density. Furthermore, the study of the entanglement pressure law's consequences on the early universe's expansion results in the determination of the minimum speed at which a flat region can re-enter the observable universe, as well as the potential for a previously unobservable region to become detectable through a local measurement, and ultimately, an upper limit is set on the Hubble parameter.

To investigate superconducting quantum devices, terahertz spectroscopy has been recently employed, yet its application is hindered by sample heating caused by near-field terahertz probing. In this study, we will present results from terahertz near-field microscopy applied to a terahertz microwave resonator made from a lithiated niobium film and situated on a silicon substrate with a high dielectric constant. We will demonstrate clear imaging of the resonator in the terahertz frequency range using a photonic crystal-based near-field terahertz microscopy system. Notably, we found that the near-field terahertz probing causes significant local heating of the superconducting film, which can impact the performance of quantum devices. To overcome this issue, we will present a method for cooling the sample by attaching it to a sapphire substrate with high thermal conductivity instead of a high dielectric constant silicon substrate. This enhancement in heat dissipation allows for the use of terahertz spectroscopy on superconducting devices without compromising the available quantum states.

A review of recent research on Venus's atmospheric characteristics reveals promising opportunities for upcoming space missions. Notable recent studies reveal long-range variations in the composition of the Venusian atmosphere. Furthermore, the complexities of the data gathered are well-suited for advanced space technologies. The research staff at the Venus Express satellite mission uncovered long-range fluctuations in the amount of sulfur dioxide in the Venusian atmosphere over the course of a year. In addition, scientists are investigating the role of high-altitude winds in the upper atmosphere in influencing these fluctuations. The surface data collected by the Veneradian tracers in recent years also exhibit extended-period fluctuations in the characteristics of the Venusian atmosphere, including the electrical activity, the amount of ultraviolet light, and the composition of the lower atmosphere, including the amount of acetylene and methane. Over the course of a year, these fluctuations may indicate the presence of chemical processes occurring in the upper atmosphere that contribute to the extreme conditions found in the lower atmosphere of the planet. The long-range variability of the Venusian atmosphere over the course of a year suggests the presence of feedback mechanisms operating within the upper atmosphere that could potentially influence the composition of the lower atmosphere and the surface of the planet, with implications for the search for life on Venus.

We utilize a Bayesian approach to analyze the reliability of a nonlinear Hawkes model with Heeghamer switching mechanisms, employing MCMC sampling. A dataset comprising 1644 months of global monthly temperature changes from 1982 to 2022 is utilized for this purpose. Our results demonstrate that the generated dataset based on the nonlinear Hawkes model captures the actual dataset's statistical features effectively, including autocorrelation. Furthermore, our research indicates that a Bayesian assessment can be effectively applied to evaluate the suitability of machine learning models.

The optimization of plasma lenses requires an in-depth understanding of how they modify the polarization of a laser beam. The impact of a plasma lens on the polarization of a highly intense, short laser pulse has been investigated numerically in a plasma with a gradually changing magnetic field. The study takes into account the propagation of the laser beam using the nonlinear Maxwell's equations. The results show that a plasma lens can achieve complete polarization conversion under specific plasma conditions. The study found that plasma lenses can modify the polarization of a laser beam in a single stage, potentially allowing for the production of high-quality, synchronized particles in future facilities.

A new method has been developed to calculate the electric dipole moment of the tau lepton, utilizing the framework of Minimal Flavour Violation within the Supersymmetric Standard Model. The calculation accounts for both one-loop contributions from neutralinos and squarks, as well as contributions from Higgs bosinos and glualls through the intermediate conversion of a virtual top quark. The final results were obtained by incorporating corrections from the running of the strong coupling constant and the renormalisation of the strong interaction, using the $\overline{\text{MS}}$ scheme. The calculated values of the tau's electric dipole moment and charge radius were also determined. The calculation was performed for various parameter sets in two generations of the MSSM's scalar sector, specifically focusing on gluino-induced contributions and scalar supersymmetry breaking scenarios, including both non-universal and universal models. The final results were further analysed in comparison to previous calculations of one-loop contributions within the MSSM.

We are interested in efficiently countable error correction for rank anomalies in both post-quantum and classical coding schemes. Our work develops two decoding techniques that limit countable anomalies in coded information to those with symmetric, positive, and indefinite definite structures, utilizing both linear time preprocessing and sparse reconstruction costs. Our first technique limits solely to positive-definite errors, employing reconciliation of at most $\tau$ non-zero components in a field of size $q$, with a reconstruction cost of $\tilde O(q^\tau+\tau^{1.5}n)$, given a code of length $n$. Our second technique limits to a combination of positive and indefinite definite errors, with a reconstruction cost of $\tilde O(\tau^\alpha q^{\tau/2}+\tau^\beta n)$, where the sum of $\alpha$ and $\beta$ is less than one. Our codes can be decoded in $\tilde O(n)$ time on average when $\tau$ is constant, with a sum of $\alpha$ and $\beta$ being $\frac56$ for the rank post-quantum code and $\frac45$ for the classical code. Our counting techniques can be expanded to code anomalies that are $\ell_p$-restricted with $p \ge 2$.

In the context of a conformal field theory with global symmetry, the operator product expansion (OE4) involves the product of two primary operators resulting in a sum of contributions from various operators categorized into segments based on their conformal spin. Focusing on a specific configuration where the initial operators are in a distant position, the coefficients of two-point functions of rotating operators have been calculated. The coefficients depend on the conformal dimensions and spin of the initial operators as well as that of the rotating operators. The resulting coefficient formula has been determined in relation to the conformal block parameters in the four-point function of external identical operators. The relationship has been examined and its consistency with previous research has been confirmed.

In 1992, Gelfand and MacPherson developed a combinatorial approach to calculating Pontrjagin classes through reduction modulo 2, a combinatorial method that yielded an explicit formula now known as the GMP formula. Although initially formulated for a singular cohomology theory, we adapt and prove this combinatorial approach for complex cobotism, where it results in the gennerealization of the GMP formula called the GMMM formula.

Observations of distant galaxies are significantly influenced by supernovae, and their spectroscopic and photometric data provide valuable insights into their chemical composition and physical characteristics. Recently, SN 2020jfo, located in the galaxy SDSS150530.33+111823.2, was discovered by the Chinese Apache Point Observatory Galactic Evolution Experiment. It was initially classified as a Type II supernova, and it remained in its photospheric phase for an unusually long time, a period that lasted 140 days for SN 2020jfo, which is three times the average duration for supernovae in spiral galaxies. By analyzing 32 spectra and conducting 20 photometric measurements across various wavelength filters, we were able to examine the evolution of the supernova's expansion, the absorption and scattering of light, and the synthesis of elements. The analysis revealed that SN 2020jfo had a mass of hydrogen in its outer layer that was 0.77 times that of its mass in elements, and it experienced significant loss of material over time as a result of radiation pressure. The analysis also showed that SN 2020jfo's expansion rate slowed down as a result of the radiation pressure, and its light curve showed a longer plateau period than is typically observed for Type II supernovae found in spiral galaxies.

To create an effective broad-field X-ray monitoring system, a new design combining a lobster-eye lens array with a curved focal plane and baffle system is proposed. This concept is particularly suitable for BGO scintillator-based X-ray detectors. The research demonstrates that a 1m diameter system can achieve a sensitive field of view of 2.4 sr with a 10 degree FWHM angular resolution and a 1 keV energy resolution, making it ideal for detecting bright X-ray transients. A 0.5m diameter variant with a reduced 25 degree angular field of view is also feasible. The concept is further explored in the context of BGO-based detectors for a 1m diameter system, and the research provides a detailed design for a 10 degree angular field of view variant.

The study of the cosmic speed field (ScField) offers a novel approach to the dark matter problem by introducing two theoretical constructs, including the concept that dark matter is not a substance but a field representing the maximum speed of light in the universe's spacetime. To investigate the functional relationship between the ScField and the distribution of dark matter halos, this research employs a random forest (RF) regression model to analyze the relationship between the ScField and the properties of dark matter halos, specifically their masses across different cosmological simulations. The results indicate that an SCField strength parameter can be accurately predicted from the masses of dark matter halos with high precision, an insight that tree-based regression models have consistently demonstrated across various simulations of the formation of dark matter. Furthermore, an inverse relationship has been found between the masses of the halos and the SCField in the SPerC simulation of the formation of massive halos, an observation that supports predictions made based on the ScField theory and previous research findings. The study also highlights the utility of artificial intelligence in exploring the functional relationships between dark matter halos and other complex, non-linear phenomena.

We reformulated the approach to formulate the equilibrium equations for a rotating star in general relativity, adopting a natural orpobit approach. This new method enables the integration of a first-order system of differential equations, facilitating the use of numerical techniques for solving the structure of a rotating star. By redefining key variables in a dimensionless manner, we established a connection between natural and geometric coordinates, resulting in an explicit expression for the geometric coordinate. This allows us to solve for the star's structure in terms of natural coordinates and obtain the physical properties of a star from its non-rotating counterpart. Our method was demonstrated using the dimensionless form of the rotating star's equilibrium equations, employing the theac11 equation of state and both barotropic and barotropeless models. Our results show that our reformulated approach yields accurate representations of both stable and unstable stars, with results that closely mirror those obtained through conventional methods.
